word-visa.t: You need a {visa} to enter the country.
My {visa} is valid for three months.
She applied for a tourist {visa} online.

word-residence-permit.t: He has a {residence permit} for two years.
I need to renew my {residence permit}.
The office issued her {residence permit} yesterday.

word-permanent-residence.t: After five years, you can apply for {permanent residence}.
They have {permanent residence} but not citizenship yet.
{Permanent residence} lets you live here without a time limit.

word-temporary-residence.t: She has {temporary residence} while she studies here.
{Temporary residence} is granted for one year at a time.
He applied for {temporary residence} after getting a job.

word-work-permit.t: You cannot start the job without a {work permit}.
Her {work permit} allows her to work full time.
The company helped him get a {work permit}.

word-citizenship.t: He applied for {citizenship} after ten years.

word-naturalization.t: He took a test as part of his {naturalization}.

word-immigration.t: She is a lawyer who handles {immigration} cases.

word-immigration-office.t: We have an appointment at the {immigration office} at nine.
The {immigration office} is closed on Fridays.
Go to the {immigration office} to get your card.

word-consulate.t: The {consulate} is downtown, near the park.
I called the {consulate} to ask about my passport.
She lost her passport and went to the {consulate}.

word-signature.t: Please put your {signature} at the bottom.

word-official-stamp.t: The clerk put an {official stamp} on the page.
You need an {official stamp} from the city office.

word-original-document.t: Please bring the {original document}, not a copy.
I lost the {original document} when I moved.
The office will return your {original document} today.

word-certified-copy.t: I need a {certified copy} of my diploma.
A simple photocopy is not a {certified copy}.

word-sworn-translator.t: The embassy only accepts papers from a {sworn translator}.
She works as a {sworn translator} for the court.

word-notary.t: We signed the contract in front of a {notary}.

word-apostille.t: This document needs an {apostille} before we can use it abroad.
The {apostille} is attached to the back page.

word-legalization.t: {Legalization} of foreign documents can take weeks.
The embassy handles the {legalization} of papers.
Do I need {legalization} for my diploma?

word-birth-certificate.t: The baby's {birth certificate} arrived in the mail.
My {birth certificate} has a spelling mistake.

word-marriage-certificate.t: We need a copy of your {marriage certificate}.
They got their {marriage certificate} at the city hall.
She keeps her {marriage certificate} in a safe.

word-criminal-record-certificate.t: I asked the police for a {criminal record certificate}.
The {criminal record certificate} must not be older than three months.
Do you need a {criminal record certificate} for this job?

word-health-insurance.t: My employer pays for my {health insurance}.
{Health insurance} is required for all residents.

word-proof-of-address.t: A bank statement can be {proof of address}.
I need {proof of address} to open an account.
Send us {proof of address} by Friday.

word-proof-of-income.t: The landlord asked for {proof of income}.
Your pay stubs are good {proof of income}.
Bring {proof of income} from the last three months.

word-passport-photo.t: Where can I get a {passport photo} taken?
Attach one {passport photo} to the form.

word-fingerprints.t: They took my {fingerprints} at the office.
The police found {fingerprints} on the door.
You must give your {fingerprints} when you apply.

word-fee.t: Is there a {fee} for this service?
You must pay the {fee} before your appointment.

word-extension.t: I applied for an {extension} of my visa.

word-renew.t: I have to {renew} my passport this year.

word-valid.t: Your passport must be {valid} for six months.
This ticket is {valid} for one day.

word-invalid.t: The form is {invalid} without a signature.
Your card is {invalid} because it expired.
The system said my password was {invalid}.

word-approve.t: The office will {approve} your request soon.
The city council must {approve} the plan.

word-reject.t: She was sad when they {rejected} her visa.

word-appeal.t: You can {appeal} the decision within thirty days.
She plans to {appeal} the court's decision.
We will {appeal} if they refuse again.

word-ministry.t: She works at the {ministry} of education.

word-municipality.t: Our {municipality} has about fifty thousand people.

word-address-registration.t: {Address registration} is required within two weeks.
You need a lease for {address registration}.

word-register-address.t: You must {register your address} within a week.
Did you {register your address} after you moved?
I will {register my address} at the town hall.

word-deregister.t: Don't forget to {deregister} before you leave the country.
She had to {deregister} at her old address.
I {deregistered} from the city last month.

word-tax-number.t: I need a {tax number} to start work.
Please write your {tax number} on the form.
The bank asked for my {tax number}.

word-personal-id-number.t: Every citizen has a {national ID number}.

word-residence-card.t: I lost my {residence card} on the train.
The new {residence card} arrives in two weeks.

word-asylum.t: She applied for {asylum} after the war began.

word-refugee.t: The family came to this country as {refugees}.
He has lived here as a {refugee} for years.
Volunteers help every {refugee} find a home.

word-family-reunification.t: {Family reunification} allows spouses to live together.
He applied for {family reunification} to bring his wife.
The process of {family reunification} can take a year.

word-social-security-number-us.t: You need a {Social Security number} to work in the US.
Never share your {Social Security number} online.
The form asks for your {Social Security number}.

word-green-card-us.t: She won a {green card} in the lottery.
He has had a {green card} for ten years.
A {green card} lets you work in the US.
